description: Cross the Welland into a town shaped by wool fortunes, towering churches and curious characters.
short_description: Hunt wool merchants, an extraordinary grave and five centuries of honey-coloured stone.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 12+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A compact central walk with one short out-and-back across Town Bridge.

before_you_go.terrain: A compact central walk with one short out-and-back across Town Bridge.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Public routes throughout; some cobbles or historic paving may be uneven.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Supportive, grippy walking shoes are recommended.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the final venue’s current dog policy.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Usually possible, though cobbles and uneven paving may be uncomfortable.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin where the Great North Road steps over a river and into a stone town.
stops.Hint_1: Find Stamford's central road crossing over the River Welland.
stops.Hint_2: Stand on Town Bridge between St Mary's Hill and High Street St Martin's.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The River Welland historically divided Stamford from Stamford Baron to the south. The Great North Road crossed here, helping the town prosper from stagecoaches long after its medieval wool trade had made local merchants wealthy.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: South of the water, find a church guarding noble Cecils and a man once measured in stones - fifty-three of them.
stops.Hint_1: Continue a short way south along High Street St Martin's.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the church on the left; Daniel Lambert's grave is in its churchyard.
stops.Unlock_Fact: St Martin's is a remarkably complete Perpendicular Gothic church containing tombs of the Cecil family from nearby Burghley House. Its churchyard holds Daniel Lambert, who weighed 52 stone 11 pounds when he died in Stamford in 1809 and was once celebrated as the heaviest man in recorded history.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Return north and find a spire raised by wool money, watched by stone saints and blind arches.
stops.Hint_1: Cross the river again and head towards Red Lion Square.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the church on All Saints' Place with a tall crocketed spire.
stops.Unlock_Fact: All Saints' has pre-Conquest origins. Its tower and spire were added in the 15th century with support from the wealthy Browne family, whose fortune came from the wool trade. Look for the unusual blind arcading along the south wall.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a hospital with no wards, founded when wool paid for beds, prayers and bread.
stops.Hint_2: Find the medieval courtyard building bearing William Browne's name.
stops.Unlock_Fact: William Browne, a rich wool merchant, founded Browne's Hospital in 1475 as an almshouse for ten poor men and two poor women. It remains a residential charity, with a chapel and an upper guild hall behind its historic frontage.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish where timber, stone and fire have survived since the thirteenth century - now with ale and pizza inside.
stops.Hint_1: Continue east along St Paul's Street.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the historic pub at number 12, named The Tobie Norris.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The Tobie Norris is a pub and restaurant inside a building dating back to the 13th century. Its old rooms, beams and fireplaces make a fitting final chapter to Stamford's stone-and-wool story - and somewhere to end with food or a drink.
